title: Add setup and exec-json worker timeouts
instructions:
Implement only Slice B from references/initiatives/post-review-worker-execution-closure.md. Use that initiative document as read-only source-of-truth for this slice. Slice A is already accepted and cleaned. Do not start Slice C.

Purpose:
- Add bounded timeout behavior to the shared command runner, setup commands, and the exec-json worker runtime path.
- Do not implement Codex SDK stream timeout in this slice except for passing through the workerTimeoutMs input shape needed by the shared WorkerRuntimeAdapter contract. Slice C owns actual codex-sdk stream timeout behavior.

Required behavior:
- Add optional TaskSpec fields setupTimeoutMs?: number and workerTimeoutMs?: number.
- Extend CommandRunResult with timeout evidence: timedOut?: boolean, timeoutMs?: number, and timeoutDetails?: a small structured object with a deterministic timeout reason and signal.
- Add timeoutMs support to runCommand(command, { cwd, timeoutMs }). Without timeoutMs, preserve current behavior.
- On command timeout, terminate the process group when possible, fall back to child.kill, use a short bounded cleanup grace, return exitCode 124, and preserve stdout/stderr emitted before timeout.
- Run setup commands sequentially with task.setupTimeoutMs ?? a deterministic default of 60_000 ms. Stop after the first non-zero or timed-out setup result.
- Ensure setup failure or timeout prevents worker runtime dispatch.
- Pass task.workerTimeoutMs ?? a deterministic default of 1_200_000 ms through executeWorkerDispatch to the runtime adapter.
- Have the exec-json adapter call runCommand with workerTimeoutMs so exec-json worker runtime timeout is enforced and recorded.
- Update closed TaskSpec validator surfaces only where they would otherwise reject setupTimeoutMs or workerTimeoutMs. Keep this minimal; do not broaden validator semantics beyond accepting finite positive timeout fields if needed.

Required tests:
- runCommand without timeout preserves existing stdout, stderr, exit code, and timing behavior.
- runCommand with timeout returns exitCode 124, timedOut true, timeoutMs, and timeoutDetails.
- runCommand timeout captures stdout/stderr emitted before timeout.
- SIGTERM-ignoring commands return within a bounded cleanup window.
- setup commands stop after timeout and worker runtime adapter is not called.
- exec-json runtime timeout returns timeout evidence.
- Existing setup command order/failure behavior still passes.
- Existing codex dispatch and worker dispatch tests still pass.
- If closed TaskSpec validator surfaces are touched, add or update focused tests proving setupTimeoutMs and workerTimeoutMs are accepted without broadening unrelated schema fields.

Stop conditions:
- Stop and report rework if the implementation requires adding CLI flags or a new command surface.
- Stop and report rework if the implementation weakens existing verification quality policy.
- Stop and report rework if timeout evidence cannot be preserved through CommandRunResult.
- Stop and report rework if setup timeout still allows worker runtime dispatch.
- Stop and report rework if actual codex-sdk stream timeout implementation is required; that belongs to Slice C.

Do not edit task templates, docs, lifecycle artifacts, merge/cleanup logic, lesson promotion code, dashboard/daemon/remote behavior, writerCap, hidden memory, Graphify integration, or LLM semantic verification. End with exactly one HARNESS_RESULT line.
